maria: Quick question for the group — I'm drafting a rollout for feature flag `use-prefix-cache` and want to confirm how scope inheritance resolves.
ben: TL;DR: nearest explicit override wins. If route has no value, it inherits from model -> project -> org in that order.
kevin: Can we get a small example? sometimes the docs feel fuzzy around 'unset' vs 'null'.
maria: Example: org=false, project=true, model=false, route=unset => effective should be model:false (so overall false)
jess: Correct. Route only takes effect if explicitly set. Unset means delegate up chain.
ben: Also check the console: unset is shown as "inherit" not blank. We added that UI change last quarter.
kevin: One more nuance — what about canary audiences? If project=true but route has canary=true (audience=5%), do we treat that as an override even if route flag boolean is unset?
maria: Route-level canary config is considered an explicit override when any audience/rules are present. So a route-level rule with 5% will win even if boolean is unset at route.
jess: Implementation detail: evaluation order is
```
1. route-level rules / audiences
2. explicit route boolean
3. model-level rules/boolean
4. project-level
5. org-level default
```
kevin: Good to call out that rules (audiences) are evaluated before booleans at the same scope — that's how gradual rollouts work.
ben: Also double-check guardrails: the rollout service will auto-block a route rollout if latency delta > 20% or error rate spikes. Rollout-Bot emits alerts to #incidents and the route owner.
rollout-bot: [notice] Canary started for route "api/v1/parse" (5% traffic). Monitoring hooks: latency, 5xx, model-quality-regressions.
maria: If we want org->project fallback for telemetry, do we have a single canonical log field for resolved_scope? i.e., what scope produced the final value.
jess: yes, we log `resolved_scope` and `resolved_value` in the evaluation trace. Searchable in Console's event stream.
kevin: One operational ask — if someone wants to flip a flag temporarily at project level for a hotfix, is it safe to leave route unset? Will it affect existing canaries?
ben: It will only affect routes that don't have a route-level rule. Routes with explicit canaries remain. So hotfix via project-level is safe for broad change but won't override per-route canaries.
maria: Great. Action items: jess to add a short note in the flag docs about rule vs boolean precedence; ben will add a brief example in the console tooltip; kevin will validate with a small integration test for `resolved_scope` logging.
jess: Ack, I'll add a doc PR. Ben, ping me if you want the tooltip copy.
ben: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
